page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.t6-c2m1.large is a shared burstable instance positioned for entry-level computational requirements with intermittent CPU demands. The instance operates on the x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. It provisions two virtual CPUs mapped to a single physical core via hyperthreading, alongside 1.0 GB of total memory, establishing a lean allocation of 0.5 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated local disk storage, requiring network-attached storage for persistent workloads, and features a baseline network bandwidth of 0 Gbps without bundled public IPv4 addresses. Virtualization is delivered through KVM, with support for instruction sets including AVX, AVX-512, and AES.

Benchmark evaluations highlight the constraints inherent to the shared, burstable design of ecs.t6-c2m1.large. The instance generated a stress-ng single-core score of 1253.28 and a multi-core score of 2345.98, placing it in the lower percentiles among evaluated systems. Compute-bound operations recorded a PassMark CPU score of 1116.23, reflecting its burst credit CPU allocation model. Memory throughput measures 185.29 GB/sec on small cached blocks (16 KB) but drops to 0.1 GB/sec on uncached 256 MB read transfers, indicating severe memory bottlenecks when operations exceed cache boundaries. Network and service benchmarks recorded static web serving throughput of 2.67 GB/sec and Redis SET operations at 1.0 million operations per second.

Given its minimal memory capacity and shared compute allocation, this instance represents a cost-effective platform for low-overhead tasks that do not sustain continuous processor utilization. The absence of local NVMe storage and dedicated baseline network bandwidth reinforces its reliance on low-demand execution profiles. The configuration fits non-critical lightweight tasks, including minor dev-test sandbox environments, basic cron automations, low-volume static web serving, and low-concurrency network proxies.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.t6-c2m1.large is an entry-tier burstable virtual machine designed for lightweight, non-continuous workloads. Built on the x86_64 architecture and powered by a 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8269CY processor, the instance allocates two burstable vCPUs across a single physical core. System resources are tightly capped at 1.0 GB of RAM, offering 0.5 GB per vCPU, with no onboard local storage, zero dedicated baseline network bandwidth, and zero integrated GPUs. Synthetic benchmarks place both single-core and multi-core CPU metrics in the lower quartile, while large-block memory read bandwidth experiences significant degradation beyond CPU cache boundaries. Redis SET operations reach 1.0 million operations per second, and static web serving achieves 2.67 GB/sec. This shared-tier profile targets cost-sensitive deployments such as minor development sandboxes, basic automated task runners, light internal utilities, and minimal static web servers that tolerate variable CPU availability.
